data.title: Astros roster analysis: Rotation.19 starters, failed signings, questions ahead - Houston Chronicle
data.content: *First in a series on the Houston Astros' 2026 season, which ended with an AL West title but a sweep in the opening round of the playoffs*. No area of the Houston Astros roster received more attention last offseason than the rotation. Only one, Imai, finished it on the Astros’ active roster, a reflection of this unit’s season-long struggles. Just three teams — the Reds, A’s and Rockies — compiled a higher rotation ERA than the Astros. Signed to a minor-league deal after a season in Japan, Lambert was released in March, re-signed with the Astros, joined their rotation in mid-April and went on to lead the team in innings (155⅔), wins (8) and pitcher bWAR (3.1). Houston’s opening day rotation was Brown, Burrows, Cristian Javier, Imai and Lance McCullers Jr. Imai, the Astros’ marquee free-agent signing, posted a 5.83 ERA in 15 starts, lost his rotation spot and ended a rough first MLB season in a mop-up role.
